posts.author: Iron_Brew
posts.body:
ANT0NS3DG3 said:
What does "increment a variable" mean?
Click to expand...
To set a variable +1 during the common event (or at any time, for that matter), but in this case this would be so that said variable corresponds with the enemy/form of the enemy in play. That way the game can track and activate conditional branches based on the number of that variable.
For example:
Far away enemy = 0
Middle distance enemy = 1
Close enemy = 2
Then at turn 0 on their troop you check what the variable is set as, and use conditional branches to transform the enemy to the appropriate form/level of closeness.

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
It would really help if you actually described in detail or showed a video of what you're talking about.
When you just say "Like in Lisa," which not everyone has played, people get different ideas in their head.
The method that
@Iron_Brew
is describing will make the enemy get larger at a specific time (either at the end of the attack or beginning of the turn) and stay that way.
I
thought from your post that you wanted the attack itself to have an animation, that the enemy would lunge toward the screen while attacking then go back at the end of the swing. You can't really do that without using plugins (e.g. Action Sequences).

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
You use an image editor to make an animation sheet of the enemy sprite getting larger and shrinking back down, then use action sequences to play the animation on top of the enemy.
Or you can use JavaScript commands to enlarge then shrink the sprite itself. The former would be easier for you to implement yourself.

Here's the notetag I did:
Code:
<setup action>
hide battle hud
</setup action>

<target action>
opacity user: 0
action animation: user
animation wait: 10
action effect: target
flash screen: red, 45
opacity user: 999
motion wait: enemies
</target action>

<finish action>
show battle hud
</finish action>
